blocks.text: Machine learning is a subfield of Data Science that enables systems to improve from experience without explicit programming. It involves analyzing patterns in data to make predictions or decisions. Large datasets are used to train models, which adapt and improve over time as new data is introduced. This technique is widely applied in modern applications, supporting automation and intelligent systems.

Instead of predefined rules, machine learning allows systems to learn from examples, identifying patterns that guide predictions. As the system processes more data, it becomes more accurate and efficient, powering smart applications and reducing manual work.

Learning from data means using past information to improve decisions. In this process, data is given as input to a learning model, which studies relationships in it. Errors are reduced through repeated training, and data becomes more accurate. Learning from data is continuous because the models update when new data is available. This process helps systems become smarter.
Difference Between Traditional Programming and Machine Learning

Traditional programming uses fixed rules written by programmers. The output is produced by following these rules. Machine learning uses data instead of fixed rules. The system learns rules automatically from data. In traditional programming, changes require new code. In machine learning, changes happen through new data. Machine learning handles complex problems better. It adapts to new situations. Figure 6.3 shows traditional programming vs machine learning

blocks.alt: Left panel, traditional programming: data and rules written by a programmer go into a program, which gives output; new behaviour needs new code. Right panel, machine learning: data and known outputs (examples) go into learning, which produces a model (the rules found); new behaviour comes from new data.

blocks.long_description: A spam filter shows the difference: a programmer cannot list every spam trick as a rule, but a model trained on thousands of labelled emails finds the patterns itself.
